subject.title: Isolated agentTurn cron: a persisted, operator-unset plugin-only toolsAllow silently strips core tools (exec/read/write) from runs — no tools.allow exists in config

question: Should a persisted job-local `toolsAllow` that appears to be a creator-derived default be automatically repaired to inherit the global tool policy, or remain an authoritative per-job restriction unless the operator explicitly clears it?
rationale: Both choices affect an authorization boundary: automatic repair can broaden existing jobs, while preserving the value leaves affected scheduled work silently unable to use expected core tools. The current report does not establish a safe universal provenance test.

options.title: Add provenance-aware repair
options.body: Recommended: retain explicit job restrictions, but identify and repair only values recorded as implicit/default-derived, with a visible Doctor or cron-editor recovery path.

options.title: Treat all persisted lists as intentional
options.body: Keep current restrictions authoritative and add diagnostics plus a manual clear action, accepting that previously stamped jobs require operator intervention.

options.title: Reset all plugin-only lists
options.body: Migrate matching lists to inherited policy, but accept a compatibility and permission-expansion risk for jobs that intentionally used them.

recommendation.title: Add provenance-aware repair
recommendation.body: Recommended: retain explicit job restrictions, but identify and repair only values recorded as implicit/default-derived, with a visible Doctor or cron-editor recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history points to the original job tool-allowlist feature area, making this the strongest available routing lead for the policy decision.
